title: Natural Light and Productivity: Analyzing the Impacts of Daylighting on Students' and Workers' Health and Alertness
research_question: What are the impacts of natural light (daylighting) on office workers' and students' health, alertness, and scholastic performance, including considerations of timing and exposure?

participants.description: Synthesized from multiple studies involving students and workers across various settings and demographics.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Various daylighting conditions (beam sunlight, diffuse skylight, reflected light, window views, full spectrum fluorescent lights as a comparison) in office and classroom environments, as reported in the reviewed literature.

measures.construct: Synthesized from multiple studies, including physiological (e.g., vitamin D levels, cortisol, melatonin), psychological (e.g., mood, alertness, depression, stress, sleep quality, satisfaction), and performance (e.g., academic test scores, productivity, attendance, cognitive performance) measures.
measures.instrument: Various instruments and scales as reported in the reviewed literature.

implementation_implications: Applying adequate daylighting techniques in school architecture contributes to occupants' physical and emotional health.
Integrating and managing daylight properly in educational environments can lead to energy saving, high student attendance, good health, strong academic performance, and reduced student stress.
Increasing daylight exposure might be a useful intervention strategy for promoting physical activity, vitality, and performance among young students.
Schools integrating full spectrum fluorescent lights or natural light witness increased student and teacher attendance.

theory_commitments.theory_name: Non-visual effects of light on human physiology
theory_commitments.specific_claim: Light exposure, particularly natural daylight, influences human non-visual photoreceptors, thereby regulating circadian rhythms, sleep-wake cycles, and subsequent alertness and cognitive function.

mechanism_chain.description: Natural light exposure activates non-visual photoreceptors, signaling to the SCN to regulate circadian rhythms, which in turn impacts alertness and cognitive performance.

steps.to_construct: Activation of intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs)
Regulation of melatonin secretion and entrainment of circadian rhythms
Improved alertness, mental focus, and cognitive performance
